name: South Korea
targetIntake: September 2027 — Korea's Fall intake (May 2027 IB session)
tagline: A separate international track, and an academic year that starts in March
summary: Korean universities run a separate admissions track for applicants who did all their schooling outside Korea, and an IB Diploma is a normal qualification inside it: no Suneung, a small international pool, and a decision made on transcript, essays and often an interview. The Korean year starts in March, so a May 2027 IB candidate can enter in September 2027, applying on predicted grades, or in March 2028 with results in hand. Fully English-taught degrees are concentrated at Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST, GIST and specific divisions elsewhere.
whyConsider: Yonsei's Underwood International College is a genuine full-English liberal-arts college inside a major research university: 16 majors across three divisions, roughly 3,000 students from more than 70 countries.
The international admissions track is document-and-interview based, which suits an IB student who writes well, and it is separate from the brutal domestic Suneung competition.
KAIST exempts scholarship holders from tuition for eight semesters and pays a monthly living allowance, decided from the admission application with no separate form to fill in.
KAIST teaches essentially all of its undergraduate programme in English, across science, engineering and business.
Seoul is genuinely affordable compared with Tokyo, Singapore or Hong Kong once you are out of the central districts, and student dormitories are cheap and widely available.
watchOuts: The Korean academic year starts in March, and the March intake is the main one. For a May 2027 IB candidate it is not an option — you cannot matriculate in March 2027 with a diploma you sit exams for in May. The two real choices are September 2027, the smaller Fall intake, or March 2028 with results in hand.

"2027 entry" does not mean one thing in Korea, so do not read it off the top of the page and stop. Elsewhere on this site it means a European autumn start; here every date belongs to one of three different intakes — September 2027, March 2027 (already gone) and March 2028 — and the intake is named on each deadline rather than assumed. KAIST muddies even the Fall one: its own calendar calls the round the Fall Track and then says the academic year begins at the end of August 2027. Check the intake named beside a date before you plan around the date.

Every deadline that matters falls before 6 July 2027. KAIST's regular round for September 2027 closes on 14 January 2027 and decides on 25 March; Yonsei UIC's second round runs in March 2027 and decides in June. Predicted grades do all the work, and what each university does with a conditional place when results arrive is set institution by institution and is not established here.

No May 2027 IB candidate can use the 2027 Global Korea Scholarship, on either track: the round needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. Plan for 2028. The Embassy Track then depends on your nationality — the 2027 list of 74 countries included the Czech Republic, Poland, Sweden and Ukraine but not Denmark, Germany or Norway — and the University Track's UIC Program is open to every nationality, but it is science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University.
The 2028 round is expected to open around September 2027. Check the new country list for your nationality when it is published.

Check very carefully what 'English-taught' means at each university. Korea University and Sungkyunkwan advertise high English-medium course percentages, but that is a university-wide average, not a guarantee that your specific major runs in English for four years.

Yonsei UIC now requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake. An IB English A result counts, and so does a Medium of Instruction certificate from a school that teaches entirely in English; English B is not on the list. Other universities set their own rules — ask each one in writing.
The only official Korean tuition figure quoted here is KAIST's, and its page carries no price year. Ask each other university for its costs.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Confirm with su.dk before budgeting. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each university reads the IB transcript inside its own international admission track, and the category that matters is the one for applicants who completed the entire curriculum outside Korea — Seoul National University calls it 글로벌인재특별전형 II, 'those who completed the entire curriculum overseas'. None of the university pages cited here publishes a minimum IB point score.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion. Each university reads the IB transcript directly within its international admissions track. The Global Korea Scholarship publishes its own thresholds — 80 per cent on a 100-point scale, or the top 20 per cent of the class, or a CGPA at or above 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — but says nothing about how an IB transcript is read against them.
notes: The relevant Korean category is the '12-year education completed entirely outside Korea' route, which an IB Diploma from a Danish gymnasium satisfies. This is the track that removes the Suneung from the equation.

Some universities accept the IB as proof of English, others insist on IELTS or TOEFL. Yonsei UIC lists IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) among its accepted proofs, with no minimum score.
Minimum and typical IB scores are not published on any university page cited here. Anything you see quoted on an agent site should be treated as unverified.
A Korean-language requirement (TOPIK) usually applies only to Korean-taught programmes, but a few English-taught degrees ask for a TOPIK level by graduation. Check the small print.

portal.name: No central portal for the international track — apply direct to each university. Study in Korea (NIIED) is the official information portal.

deadlines.label: KAIST Regular Admissions, Fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: KAIST's own timeline says this round's "Academic Year Begins: End of August, 2027". Opens 10 November 2026. The recommendation letter has a later deadline of its own, 21 January 2027. Decision 25 March 2027, before IB results on 6 July 2027. KAIST's other round, Early Admissions (22 September to 22 October 2026), leads to a start at the end of February 2027 and cannot be used by a May 2027 candidate.

deadlines.label: Yonsei UIC 2nd Round, Fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: UIC states "International students can matriculate either in March or in September"; its 2nd Round is the Fall 2027 entry term and is published only as "March, 2027" for application and documents, with interview and notification in June 2027. The 1st Round (Spring 2027 entry) closed on 22 September 2026. Application fee KRW 150,000, or USD 150 through the Common App.

deadlines.label: Korea University Fall 2027 application
deadlines.notes: Korea University's international admission guide lists Spring 2027 and Fall 2027 side by side and gives every Fall 2027 row — online application, materials submission, result release, registration — as "(TBA)". Korea University admits internationals twice a year and announces the September round late: its Spring 2027 equivalent ran 3 to 31 August 2026, about seven months ahead of the March start. Submitted through Uwayapply, not the university's own site, which is where people lose the deadline. This was the position on 23 September 2026.

deadlines.label: Embassy Track online application, 2027 GKS-U

readerAccess.reason: The 2027 round needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026, which a May 2027 IB candidate cannot supply, whatever their passport.

deadlines.notes: The guidelines give the window as "September 15, 2026 (Tue.), 11:00 – September 30, 2026 (Wed.), 18:00", Korea Standard Time; the closing end of it is the date recorded here. Closed to a May 2027 IB candidate of any nationality, because an applicant expected to graduate "must submit a graduation certificate (or a degree certificate) and a transcript by December 31, 2026". The dates are in the PDF "2027 GKS-U Application Guidelines (English) 0914.pdf" attached to NIIED's notice page, https://www.studyinkorea.go.kr/en/plan/gksNoticeRead.do?bbsId=BBSMSTR_000000000461&nttId=4522.

deadlines.label: University Track application, 2027 GKS-U
deadlines.notes: NIIED gives the University Track application period as "September–November 2026, according to each university's own schedule" and tells applicants to check each university's own announcement for the period, the submission method and the documents — so there is no single date and there cannot be one. The UIC Program is the only part of GKS open to every nationality: the guidelines mark its Eligible Countries as "All countries worldwide", 100 Bachelor's and Associate places across 13 named institutions, all of them science and engineering, and none of them Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University. Applying on more than one track voids the application. Find each university's own GKS announcement for its deadline. The track's dates are in the guidelines PDF, not on NIIED's notice page.

deadlines.label: First international round for the March 2028 intake
deadlines.notes: The alternative to September 2027, and the only Korean intake a May 2027 IB candidate can apply to holding an actual diploma. Nothing is published yet: as of 23 September 2026 the only guideline on SNU's international admissions page is "Admissions for Undergraduate, Spring 2027", with no Spring 2028 document and no "to be announced" placeholder beside it. In the 2027 cycle the equivalent rounds ran 6–9 July 2026 at Seoul National, 3–31 August 2026 at Korea University and 26 August–22 September 2026 at Yonsei UIC; those dates are not a guide to 2028's. SNU's dates are in the guideline PDF linked from its page, which is in Korean apart from the cover.

steps: From September 2026, check each target university's 'Admission for International Students' or 'Overseas Korean and Foreigner Special Admission' page — this is a different page from the domestic admissions site, and often a different subdomain.
Confirm whether your intended major genuinely runs in English for all four years, in writing, from the department rather than the marketing page.

Decide between September 2027 and March 2028. March 2027 is not available to you: it is Korea's main intake, but its rounds closed in the summer and early autumn of 2026 and it starts before you have sat your exams.
Prepare the standard international pack: IB transcript and predicted grades, a self-introduction essay, a study plan, references, proof of your and your parents' nationality, and financial evidence.

If you want the Global Korea Scholarship, plan for the 2028 round: no May 2027 IB candidate can use 2027's. Read the invited-country list first — the Embassy Track depends on your nationality, while the University Track's UIC Program is open to every nationality but covers only science and engineering at thirteen named universities. Applying on more than one track voids the application.
Once admitted, the university issues a Certificate of Admission; you apply for a D-2 student visa at the Korean embassy and register for an Alien Registration Card within 90 days of arrival.
application.selectionNotes: Selection in the international track is holistic: transcript, essays, references and usually an online interview. The international track is a separate pool from the domestic route. UIC, KAIST and SNU are selective.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated rather than widespread. Yonsei UIC (16 majors), KAIST, POSTECH (a fully English-taught curriculum for international undergraduates since Fall 2026), UNIST and GIST, and selected divisions at Korea University, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha and Kyung Hee. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per university. Yonsei UIC requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake, and accepts an IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) result with no minimum score, a TOEFL, IELTS or CEFR certificate, or a Medium of Instruction certificate for a school curriculum taught entirely in English. UNIST asks for an English test report. Elsewhere, ask each admissions office.
notes: You do not need Korean to be admitted to an English-taught programme, but you will need it to live well, to work part-time and to do internships.
Most universities run free or heavily subsidised Korean language classes for their own international students.
The Global Korea Scholarship includes a full year of Korean language training before the degree begins — one of the reasons it is worth more than its cash value.

tuitionEuEea.value: Korea does not differentiate by nationality — international students pay the same published tuition as Korean students at most universities.

costs.applicationFee: Charged by each university: Yonsei UIC KRW 150,000 (USD 150 through the Common App) and Seoul National University KRW 70,000 for the 2027 cycle. Check the others on each university's page.
notes: KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW a semester, national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW, all per semester. Its page states no academic year, and these figures do not apply to any other university.

The structure to expect: tuition is charged per semester and varies sharply by faculty, with medicine and engineering highest and humanities lowest. Private universities (Yonsei, Korea, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha, Hanyang) charge considerably more than the national universities.
Most universities award an automatic partial tuition scholarship to admitted international students, often tied to grades — ask what the standing award is before comparing sticker prices.

Dormitory places are cheap and usually available to first-year international students. Off-campus renting in Korea involves a large jeonse or wolse key deposit that is difficult to raise from abroad — take the dormitory.

funding: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), run by NIIED — the Korean government's scholarship for undergraduate degrees, and smaller than it looks from Denmark. The 2027 round covers tuition of up to 5m KRW a semester, a Korean language year costing 5.2m KRW, airfare, and an allowance of 13.56m KRW in the language year and 14.4m KRW a year during the degree, over five to seven years. No May 2027 IB graduate can use the 2027 round, on either track, because it requires a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026 — plan for 2028. Then the Embassy Track depends on your nationality (the 2027 list of 74 countries left out Denmark), and the University Track's UIC Program, science and engineering at thirteen named universities, is open to every nationality.

University international-student scholarships: most Korean universities award an automatic tuition reduction to admitted international students, frequently renewable on GPA. Ask each admissions office for the standing rate, since it changes the real price materially.

The KAIST Scholarship exempts an admitted international undergraduate from tuition for eight semesters and pays 350,000 KRW a month plus medical insurance. There is no separate application — you tick a box on the admission form — and it is held on a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.
Yonsei, Korea University and SNU all operate named merit awards for high-performing international entrants. Ask each for the terms.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: Part-time work is permitted on a D-2 visa with permission from the immigration office, but the hour limits and the requirement for a TOPIK level vary — confirm with Korea Immigration Service.
workRights: Students on a D-2 visa may work part-time only after obtaining permission from the immigration office, with hour limits that in recent years have been tied to Korean language proficiency (TOPIK level) and academic standing. Confirm the current limits with the Korea Immigration Service before relying on part-time earnings.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. You need a D-2 student visa, applied for at the Korean embassy in Copenhagen with the Certificate of Admission issued by your university, proof of funds, and a criminal-record and tuberculosis check. Within 90 days of arrival you register for an Alien Registration Card at the local immigration office — you cannot open a bank account or get a phone contract without it.
housing: University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and allocated with the admission. The private market in Seoul requires a large up-front deposit (jeonse or wolse) that is impractical to arrange from Denmark. Apply for the dormitory the moment your offer arrives — places at Yonsei and Korea University are oversubscribed.
healthcare: International students staying more than six months are enrolled in Korea's National Health Insurance Service, with a monthly premium deducted or billed. It is compulsory and it is good — Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. Your EHIC does not apply.

institutions.name: Yonsei University — Underwood International College
institutions.englishBachelors: 16 majors, all taught in English, across three divisions: Underwood (comparative literature, economics, international studies, political science and IR, life science and biotechnology); Humanities Arts and Social Sciences (Asian studies, culture and design management, information and interaction design, creative technology management, justice and civil leadership, quantitative risk management, science technology and policy, sustainable development and cooperation); and Integrated Science and Engineering (nano science, energy and environmental science, bio-convergence).
institutions.note: A liberal-arts college of about 3,000 students from more than 70 countries, inside Yonsei. The first two years are on the Songdo campus near Incheon, then Sinchon in central Seoul.

institutions.name: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Essentially the entire undergraduate programme is taught in English across science, engineering, business and the College of Liberal Arts and Convergence Science.
institutions.note: A science and technology institute in Daejeon where undergraduates choose their major at the end of first year. Known for generous scholarship support, including for international students; confirm the current terms with the admissions office.

institutions.name: Seoul National University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. SNU runs a large share of its graduate teaching in English, but undergraduate English-medium provision is partial and varies by college. Verify programme by programme before applying.
institutions.note: Very hard to enter through the domestic route, which makes the separate international track valuable. Its undergraduate curriculum is not systematically English-medium.

institutions.name: Korea University
institutions.englishBachelors: A substantial share of courses are taught in English, particularly in Business, International Studies, Political Science and Economics, but few majors are guaranteed 100% English for four years. Verify with the department.
institutions.note: One of the 'SKY' trio with SNU and Yonsei, where the Division of International Studies is the most reliably English-taught part. Applications run through Uwayapply, a shared national platform, rather than the university's own site.

institutions.name: Sungkyunkwan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Global Business Administration, Global Economics, Global Leader (law and policy) and several science and engineering tracks are taught substantially or wholly in English. Verify individually.
institutions.note: Traces itself to a Confucian academy founded in 1398, but is funded by Samsung and thoroughly modern. Its semiconductor and software programmes come with direct Samsung recruitment pipelines.

institutions.name: Ewha Womans University
institutions.englishBachelors: The Division of International Studies in Scranton College (International Studies and Global Korean Studies) is taught entirely in English; other faculties are largely Korean-medium.
institutions.note: A women's university central to modern Korean history. Its Division of International Studies has taught in English since 2001; admission is open to women only.

institutions.name: Hanyang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected engineering, business and international studies tracks. Check with the university.
institutions.note: A private university known for engineering, with a strong start-up culture. Its engineering curriculum is unusually practical.

institutions.name: Pohang University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Since Fall 2026 POSTECH admits international undergraduate freshmen, outside the domestic quota, to a 100% English-taught curriculum, with the same tuition waiver as Korean students.
institutions.note: A small, research-intensive science institute founded by the POSCO steel company, with a famously high staff-to-student ratio. Its international undergraduate track is new; the first cohort entered in autumn 2026.

institutions.name: Sogang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected business, economics and international studies courses. Check with the university.
institutions.note: A small Jesuit university in Seoul with a reputation for rigour. Its well-known Korean-language institute helps if you want to learn the language properly alongside a degree.

institutions.name: Kyung Hee University
institutions.englishBachelors: College of International Studies and selected hospitality and business tracks. Check with the university.
institutions.note: Large and internationally oriented, with many international students. Unusual strengths in hospitality management and traditional Korean medicine.

institutions.name: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: UNIST teaches its undergraduate programme in English and has published Fall 2027 admission guidelines for international applicants.
institutions.note: A science institute in Ulsan, Hyundai's industrial city, teaching its undergraduate programme in English. Undergraduates enter undeclared and choose a track after a common first year.

institutions.name: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: The undergraduate College teaches in English with a common curriculum before major selection. Verify current policy.
institutions.note: A small research institute in the south-west with a liberal-arts-inflected science curriculum: every undergraduate takes humanities alongside the science core. About 200 undergraduates a year.

institutions.name: Handong Global University
institutions.englishBachelors: A large share of teaching is in English, including the International Studies, Languages and Literature and Global Management tracks. Check with the university.
institutions.note: A Christian university with an explicitly international mission and an unusual undeclared-entry structure: students choose a major at the end of the first year and may double-major freely. Considerably more accessible than the Seoul universities.

institutions.name: Chung-Ang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected business, economics and international tracks. Check with the university.
institutions.note: Known for film, drama and the performing arts; many Korean screen actors and directors trained here. A strong choice if the draw is Korea's cultural industries.
